doc.title: Laurence Juber interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 21, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Lockdown in March and Perry Botkin Jr. and Sr.
summary: He recalls the March 2020 cancellations and lockdown, then talks about his friend Perry Botkin Jr. and Perry Botkin Sr., Bing Crosby's musical director and link between New York and L.A. studio guitar.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: It happened very quickly. It was funny because I saw that there were going to be some travel limitations and I was actually, I was ready to get a new car, and I think it was March 10th I got a Subaru Crosstrek anticipating that I’d probably be doing a lot of driving in California. Because I already had to cancel a tour of Taiwan. And then when I went out to dinner with a friend on the 12th of March and learned that he had a number of colleagues who had been hospitalized because they’d been on a skiing trip to northern Italy, and realizing that it was in the community already. And then that weekend I had three southern California gigs, all of which got cancelled, kind of the day before. And at that point it was like okay we went into lockdown before the city went into lockdown, which for a while was really uncomfortable because we couldn’t see the grandchildren. Since then we’ve now, they come over to swim and we just keep a distance. And there’s a little bit of socializing going on, actually it’s an interesting one, and I’m having a second socially distanced lunch with a friend of mine who is 87 now, Perry Botkin Jr. He is a composer, he is a TV composer who wrote “Nadia’s Theme” which is the theme from “The Young and the Restless” that Nadia Comaneci used, which was originally actually a source cue from I think “Mork & Mindy” because Perry did the music for “Mork & Mindy” at Paramount. But what’s really interesting is that his dad, Perry Botkin Sr. was Bing Crosby’s musical director for 17 years, and kind of stepped into Eddie Lang’s role, because Eddie Lang and Bing Crosby had a very close relationship. And Perry Botkin really, I think, and I’m kind of learning this from talking to Perry Jr. and from just doing my own research that Perry was kind of the link between the New York jazz studio guitar players, like Eddie Lang, and the L.A. studio players. Because Perry kind of made that move and really became very established in L.A. in the pre-Wrecking Crew era, ended up writing music, he wrote music for “The Munsters” and was, there’s some interesting video of him on YouTube. He was in the “Birth of the Blues” movie with Bing Crosby, which I think is kind of an idealized story of the crossover of jazz from black to white musicians you know, with the — what’s the jazz band that put out the first kind of supposedly legitimate.
Oh yea, the Original Dixieland Jazz Band.
